REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - FEBRUARY 8, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 8,
2024, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Pro Tem Naresh Solanki.

 4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

 5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council honoring:

  Dr. Natalie Sartin, English Department Associate Professor and Black/African Studies Chair,
  Cerritos Community College (Black History Month).

 5B.  An informational report to the Cerritos City Council regarding the Los Angeles County
  Metropolitan Transportation Authority’s Southbound I-605 South Street off-ramp
  improvement project (COUNCIL).

  An informational report was given by Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation
  Authority (Metro) Board of Directors Member/City of Whittier Mayor Pro Tem Fernando
  Dutra and Olga Arroyo, Metro Director of Community Relations. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  Metro Director of Community Relations Olga Arroyo submitted a document (contact card)
  for the official record. (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting are
  considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted written
  correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer).

  This was an informational item and no action was taken.

 6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Mayor Barrows provided information concerning decorum during the public meeting.

  Vida Barone, City Clerk, provided the following disclaimer concerning written comments
  submitted for all agenda items: Written comments submitted by the deadline listed on the
  agenda are considered public record. Prior to the meeting, the Council/Agency members
  received full-text, unredacted copies of any written comments submitted for items listed on
  the agenda, including general public comments. Public requests for copies of the written
  comments submitted for this meeting can be made during regular business hours to the
  Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written Correspondence:

  Andrés Martínez Pais commented on behalf of the State of California Mortgage Relief

  Gail and Marty Grossman requested the City refrain from participating in global politics.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Farwa Jafri
  Edwin Morales

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Gail Grossman expressed concern regarding accessibility to the City Council Chamber for
  those with disabilities and the lack of adequate handicap parking spaces in the Civic Center
  Plaza.

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to provide information to the City
  Council concerning options for additional disabled access to City Hall/Council Chamber and
  increasing the number of disabled parking stalls at the Civic Center Plaza.

  Michael Wauschek requested the City Council take action to support a ceasefire in
  Palestine.

  Coleen Aldrich requested additional handicap parking in the Civic Center Plaza and thanked
  the City for considering the coyote Wildlife Watch Program at the January 2024 Community
  Safety Committee meeting.

  Emmanuel Ronquillo requested the City Council take action to support a ceasefire in
  Palestine.

  Christy Montaver expressed concern with actions taken against Palestinians.

  Sophia Tse provided information concerning the decline in ABC Unified School District
  enrollment.

  Margaret Villa expressed concern that Cerritos funds are being utilized to fund Israel and
  requested the City Council adopt a resolution in support of H.Res 786.

  Jay Gray expressed support for Israel’s rights to defend itself, the freedom of speech right
  in the United States, and for the City to follow its established policies. He also commented
  on the removal of the United States Constitution and other decorative items from the City
  Council Chamber, the City Treasurer position, and the Art in Public Places program.

  Mel Cortez requested the date of the next paper shredding event required to be provided by
  Athens Services and expressed concern with the street sweeping service provided by the
  same company. He displayed the “welcome kit” provided to Neighborhood Watch
  volunteers, requested residents to participate in the Wildlife Watch program, and expressed
  concern with the impact of declining ABC Unified School District enrollment on the City.

  Al Barlevy requested the City Council not take a position on the conflict occurring between
  Israel and Palestine.

  Aditya Pai requested the support of Cerritos residents in his campaign to be elected to
  represent the 45th California Congressional District.

  Bill Irhke, City Attorney, stated that the Mayor is the presiding officer during the public City
  Council meetings, and has the authority under State and local laws to govern public
  comment procedures.

  Sam Desai expressed concern with impacts that may arise in the City due to closure of local
  schools and the accountability of the Chamber of Commerce.

  Jenna Hajjar requested the City Council take action to support a ceasefire in Palestine.

  Fernando Islas requested the City Council adopt a resolution in support of H.Res 786.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Thursday, January 25, 2024, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to approve the Thursday,
  January 25, 2024, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None

  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated February 8, 2024 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to approve the Register of

  City of Cerritos  February 8, 2024  $4,399,245.95 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Award of contract for professional services to conduct a financial analysis and business plan
  in association with a City of Cerritos municipal fiber optic broadband service* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Sections 15061(b)(3) and 15378(b)(5) of the California Environmental Quality
  Act (CEQA) Guidelines, the contract is exempt from CEQA review.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, February 8, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 10

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to:

  1. Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public
  Resources Code Section 21000 et seq. (CEQA) that the proposed contract award is
  exempt from CEQA review pursuant to Sections 15061(b)(3) and 15378(b)(5) of the
  CEQA Guidelines, based on the findings set forth in the agenda report associated with
  this item;

  2. Authorize a budget amendment for the appropriation of funds in the amount of
  $230,000 from the General Fund for financial analysis and business plan services in
  association with a City of Cerritos municipal fiber optic broadband service, the new
  Citywide Fiber Optic Improvements CIP project to be included in Fiscal Year 2023-2024;

  3. Award a contract in the amount of $230,000 to CTC Technology & Energy of
  Kensington, Maryland for financial analysis and business plan services; and

  4. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute any project-related change orders,
  in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Recommendation by the Cerritos Planning Commission, on a vote of 5-0, to approve the
  following:

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING TITLE 22 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO
  THE REGULATION OF BODY ART BUSINESSES IN THE CITY OF CERRITOS, HEREIN
  REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2024-1* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines,
  this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  A staff report was given by Sabrina Chan, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Sam Desai expressed support for approval of body art businesses in the City, citing various
  cultural traditions expressed through body art.

  Written Correspondence:

  Gail Grossman expressed support for body art businesses if they remain in compliance with
  applicable health and safety provisions.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, February 8, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 10

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period and the public
  hearing closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the recommendation
  by the Cerritos Planning Commission to waive full reading of and introduce Ordinance No.
  1043, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING TITLE 22 OF THE
  CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE REGULATION OF BODY ART
  BUSINESSES IN THE CITY OF CERRITOS, HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT
  CODE AMENDMENT 2024-1 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, Item 9B was heard at this juncture of the meeting. The
  detail for Item 9B is listed in the appropriate section below.

9A.  Review and consideration to rename a City of Cerritos facility (COUNCIL).

  (Pursuant to City Council consensus, this item was considered after Item 9B concluded.)

  Staff reports were given by Sherré Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent and Bill Ihrke,
  City Attorney.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Gail Grossman expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East.

  Karen Wilson expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East and suggested an
  alternative to honor former City Manager Art Gallucci by placing a plaque in the City
  Council Chamber.

  Catherine Pascual expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East and
  requested enhancements to park facilities as an alternative.

  Coleen Aldrich expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East and the waiver of
  established City policies.

  Jay Gray expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East and the waiver of
  established City policies.

  Steve Peters expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East.

  Sean Peters expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East.

City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 10

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  Mel Cortez expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East and the waiver of
  established City policies. He submitted a document for the record, entitled, “Preserve the
  Name of Cerritos Park East.” (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting
  are considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted written
  correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer).

  Sam Desai expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East.

  Dale Meyers expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East.

  Written Correspondence:

  The following individuals expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East:

  Sue Carter
  Rosa Peters
  Murali Vasudevan
  Deborah ONeal
  Jaime Ball
  Gail and Marty Grossman
  Norma and Alan Williamson

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MAIN MOTION (HELD PENDING): It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to
  approve a one-time waiver of City Policy 7.06 – Naming and Renaming of City Facilities and
  name the hallway entrance to the main theater at the Cerritos Center for the Performing
  Arts in honor of former City Manager Art Gallucci (COUNCIL).

  (The main motion was held pending due to consideration of a substitute motion.)

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION (DID NOT PASS): It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by
  Yokoyama, to follow and adhere to the provisions of City Policy 7.06 – Naming and Renaming of
  City Facilities, which was adopted as part of the City of Cerritos Policy and Procedure Manual on
  April 28, 2022 (COUNCIL).

  The motion did not carry (2 - 3) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  Vo, Solanki, Barrows
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MAIN MOTION (CARRIED): It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to approve a
  one-time waiver of City Policy 7.06 – Naming and Renaming of City Facilities and name the
  hallway at the entrance of the main theater at the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts
  in honor of former City Manager Art Gallucci (COUNCIL).

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, February 8, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 8 of 10

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  The motion carried (3 - 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Vo, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  Johnson, Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS IN SUPPORT OF THE CERRITOS SHERIFF’S STATION
  DEPUTIES (COUNCIL).

  (Pursuant to City Council consensus, this item was considered prior to action on Item 9A.)

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written Correspondence:

  Marty and Gail Grossman expressed gratitude for the Cerritos Sheriff’s Station Deputies for
  ensuring the safety of the community.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Barrows, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2024-06, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS IN SUPPORT OF THE CERRITOS
  SHERIFF’S STATION DEPUTIES (COUNCIL); and

  2. Direct staff to distribute a signed letter of appreciation of each Cerritos Sheriff’s Station
  deputy, as set forth in the agenda report associated with this item (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal
  legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, February 8, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 9 of 10

11.  Reports

11A.  Report from City Manager/Executive Director

11A.1. An informational update regarding the City’s transportation services.

  An informational update was given by Kristin Aguila, Director of Community Development,
  on the status of the City’s transportation services and the “opt-in” Homeowner Alert
  Service (e-Notification) offered by the Los Angeles County Assessor to identify potential
  real estate fraud activity.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to work with County Supervisor
  Janice Hahn, the City’s Congressional representatives, the Southern California Association
  of Governments, and the City’s other Local and Federal resources to seek an alternative use
  and an extension for the use of the City’s $4.4 million Federal Transit Administration Bus
  and Bus Facilities grant for fixed-route transportation service.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to include a notice of the “opt-in”
  Homeowner Alert Service (e-Notification) offered by the Los Angeles County Assessor in the
  City’s water billing mailers sent to each household.

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Reports were given by Councilmembers Johnson, Vo, and Yokoyama, Mayor Pro Tem
  Solanki, and Mayor Barrows.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to place photographs of former City
  Managers in the City Hall complex.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to update and replace the U.S.
  Constitution, City map, and other framed documents in the City Council Chamber.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to provide a monthly Commission and
  Committee member attendance report to the City Council, retroactive to January 1, 2024.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the Charter Employees to research options for requiring
  the submittal of conflict of interest disclosure forms from contracted persons or firms (per
  the Political Reform Act and Levine Act) in City contracts and other applicable documents
  that are considered for approval by the City Council, Commissions, and Committees, in a
  format similar to that provided by Southern California Association of Governments, and
  include similar updates to applicable consultant forms in the Conflict of Interest Code
  during the mandated 2024 biennial review.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to schedule the Park and Recreation
  Commission to review options to replace the “spray pool” at Cerritos Park East (CPE) and
  schedule a City Council report at a future meeting to review any resulting
  recommendations.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 11:49 p.m.
